stops.title: Fillmore Auditorium
stops.body: First public show under the name Grateful Dead — Bill Graham's venue became their spiritual home.

stops.title: Human Be-In
stops.body: Thirty thousand gathered in the park — the Dead alongside Jefferson Airplane, Leary's call to tune in.

stops.title: Sunshine Daydream
stops.body: An outdoor benefit on a hot August day — peak performance, later immortalized on film.

stops.title: Winterland
stops.body: Six hundred forty-one speakers — seventy-five tons of PA. Revolutionary concert sound, then farewell.

stops.title: Barton Hall
stops.body: May eighth — widely hailed as the greatest show. Scarlet Begonias into Fire on the Mountain.

stops.title: Great Pyramids
stops.body: Three nights at the pyramids during a lunar eclipse — among the most mystical performances in rock history.
stops.photoCaption: Great Pyramid of Giza — Wikimedia Commons

stops.title: Alpine Valley
stops.body: Midwest outdoor amphitheater — a Deadhead mecca in the natural bowl of Wisconsin.

stops.title: Soldier Field
stops.body: July ninth — the last concert with Jerry Garcia. Show number two thousand three hundred eighteen.

endCard.title: The tour never really ended
endCard.body: Explore every stop in the Live Music Pilgrimage Atlas.
